answer: Require each new agent's attesters to sit at least three graph-hops apart in the existing trust graph, so a cluster of colluding fakes can't vouch for itself. Attestations carry a staked bond; if a later audit reveals the attested agent's behavior deviates from its claimed pigment of reliability, the bond is slashed. This raises an attacker's cost to forging a quorum: they must first penetrate distinct, unconnected regions of the graph, and any echo of coordinated fake vouching leaves a detectable trace across the mesa of trust history, making each successful sybil exponentially pricier.
